methods.description: Read immutable issue-pinned Git blobs; check whole-file hashes, one exact subject feature, its parent record and the declared child count. Reproduction output is streamed to stdout; no file destination is opened or modified.
methods.software: Python 3 standard library json, hashlib, pathlib, subprocess; git show
methods.units: feature and hierarchy record counts; no area or distance calculation

methods.description: Hash and parse the retained immutable Natural Earth v5.1.0 GeoJSON, find ADM0_A3 SPI exactly once, and compute SHA-256 of canonical feature geometry using sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON. Compare to the Atlas stored original_geometry_sha256 without normalizing or asserting equivalence.
methods.software: Python 3 standard library json and hashlib
methods.units: whole-file bytes, feature count, exterior-ring coordinate count, canonical JSON geometry SHA-256

conclusions.text: The dated Natural Earth v5.1.0 candidate contains the unique SPI map-unit identity and explicitly classifies it as indeterminate/disputed; it is not verified as the exact geometry used for the Atlas feature because its geometry hash differs from the stored original hash.
The physical role is supported at aggregate ice-field scale, while the exact perimeter and Atlas province-tier interpretation are not established by the reviewed glacier inventories.
The dated Natural Earth 5.1.0 source is the exact original geometry source used by Atlas.
The current demarcation status and the exact present-day sovereign side of each icefield polygon coordinate are established by the 1998 agreement and glacier inventories.
The same-name one-child province tier represents a source-supported administrative province rather than a physical feature grouping.
